newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIANS STRETCHED BY GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-RUSSIANS STRETCHED BY GERMANY.

text.p: Once-powerful Russia struggled for much of their world ice hockey championship clash with Germany on Monday before a late three-goal burst gave them a 5-1 win.
Defender Anatoly Fedotov hammered home the decisive goal to give Russia a badly needed 3-1 lead in the 47th minute.
Oleg Belov had scored the opening goal five minutes into the second period but Bradley Bergen levelled within seven minutes. Sergei Petrenko restored Russia's advantage just 36 seconds later.
German head coach George Kingston said failure by his players in man-to-man marking had provided Russia with the openings to score their second and third goals.
"Against opponents who are so good, so fast skaters, you must succeed in the covering all the time," Kingston said.
Russian head coach Igor Dimitryev said it had been a difficult and close match until the very last minute.
With 21 seconds left, Mikhail Sarmatin scored into an empty goal after Germany pulled goaltender Joeph Heiss. Alexei Morozov chipped in Russia's fifth two seconds from time.
